Name: The Debasement of the Carthaginian Silver Shekel and the Pay of Overseas Mercenaries
RagShortTexts: In the later war, after losing the silver mines of Castulo in Spain, the flow of silver into Carthage's treasury dried up
The Council of One Hundred was forced to mix large amounts of bronze, copper and lead into the silver shekel, cutting its fineness in half
Mercenaries refused the debased coins, setting off mutinies among the Danube Gallic legions and the Iberian soldiers
BaseText: In sharp contrast to Rome, which stabilized its finances in adversity with the denarius, the Carthaginian financial and monetary system suffered a devastating collapse through debasement in the later years of the war. Its traditional pure-silver coin, the 'shekel' (Shekel), had once been backed by the mines of Andalusia and New Carthage and was of very high fineness. But when Scipio Africanus took New Carthage completely and occupied the silver mines of Castulo between 209 and 206 BC, the silver supply of the Carthaginian homeland dried up at once. In extreme panic, the mint of the Council of One Hundred had to mix large amounts of copper, lead and impurities into the molten silver, so that the silver content of the circulating Carthaginian shekel plunged from 90 percent to less than 35 percent, and the faces of the coins even showed a blackened verdigris. The profit-minded mercenaries tested the coins with fire on payday and flew into a rage; several times they broke out in riots and mutinies, refusing to march and seizing the officers in charge of the baggage train, and the fighting strength of the Carthaginian army was drained away completely in the financial collapse.

Variants.Content: Look at this blackened scrap copper! Does the Carthaginian Senate want to pay us off with silver filings in muddy water and send us against the Roman javelins? Without pure silver shekels, the line will split apart by itself tomorrow!

The silver ships from Spain no longer sail, and even the rats in the treasury are fighting! If we do not mix in copper to get through this crisis, are we supposed to smash the golden statues in the temples and share them out among those greedy barbarians?

The Carthaginian empire of money is falling apart with the loss of its silver mines. Mercenaries who gathered for silver coins will surely betray their employers the moment they are handed false money.
